name: Woodland
about:
Woodland was founded in 1996 by Lynn and Pat Harker in Idaho Falls, Idaho. Pat Harker, drawing on experience from her design firm Harker Design, envisioned a resource that would serve interior designers with high-quality products, service excellence, delivery in under 12 weeks, and fair pricing. The company began with that four-part ideal and has remained privately held by its founders.

Today Woodland produces cabinetry, lighting, and upholstery as a whole-home solution for designers. The operation emphasizes custom designs and custom finishes, relying on craft and artistry rather than full automation. The facility earned the Shingo Prize in 2000 for excellence in lean manufacturing, reflecting a commitment to continuous improvement on the shop floor.

The primary customers are interior design professionals and design firms seeking tailored residential furnishings. Designers specify Woodland pieces for custom residential projects, relying on the company’s ability to translate design intent into finished cabinetry, lighting fixtures, and upholstered goods.

Woodland differentiates itself through its dedication to handcrafted custom work, a stated delivery target of under 12 weeks, and a pricing philosophy described as fair. The Shingo Prize recognition underscores a lean manufacturing culture that the company says supports both quality and responsiveness.

about:
Woodland Manufacturing operates from Meridian, Idaho, where it was founded in 2003 as a limited liability company. The business began in a garage with computer-guided saws nicknamed "The Beast," cutting wooden letters for custom signage.

Today the shop produces custom sign letters, plaques, and event displays using wood, metal (aluminum, bronze, steel, brass, copper), plastic (acrylic, foam, formed and injection-molded), and vinyl. In-house capabilities include CNC routing, laser cutting, water jet cutting, vinyl cutting, and media production. The company describes its workshop as stocked and its capabilities as virtually limitless, though it does not disclose facility size, headcount, or annual volumes.

Customers range from businesses, churches, and government offices to industrial shops and event organizers. The company notes that its clients often have a DIY attitude and confidence in designing and installing their own signage, and it supports them with installation guides and finishing tutorials.

Woodland Manufacturing emphasizes that it carries no stock inventory; every letter is handcrafted per order. It promises quotes within one business day and highlights friendly customer service, design expertise, and experienced artisans as the foundation of its approach.

name: Woodmaster Tools Inc
old_description: That’s why we can back our machines and service with the best guarantee in the industry!
about:
Woodmaster Tools Inc is based in Kansas City, Missouri, where it has built planer/molders and other woodworking machinery for over 45 years. The company does not disclose a specific founding year or founder names in its public materials, and ownership structure is not stated. It describes itself as an American manufacturer operating in the "Heart of the Heartland."

The company designs and manufactures a line of woodworking machines that includes planer/molders, drum sanders, a 4-side molder (the WM4000), a super-wide planer, and a 3-side molding attachment. It also produces custom molding knives and offers over 600 standard molding patterns. Woodmaster cites more than 200,000 customers and 150,000 satisfied owners, but does not publish facility square footage, employee count, or annual production volumes.

Woodmaster's customers are primarily small to mid-sized woodworking shops, custom millwork operations, and entrepreneurs producing items such as molding, picture frames, and specialty products like air-conditioned dog houses. The company highlights individual owners who run part-time or full-time businesses using multiple Woodmaster machines.

Woodmaster emphasizes several differentiators: a true variable feed rate on its machines, U.S. manufacture in Kansas City, custom configuration for each buyer, a 60-day money-back guarantee, a five-year limited warranty covering the entire machine including motors, and what it calls "200 years of in-house expertise" from its staff.

about:
Woodrich operates from Williamsport, Pennsylvania, where it produces handmade wood furniture using sustainably sourced local lumber. The company focuses on custom pieces built to order, with a design process that begins through live chat or text consultation.

The product line spans dining tables, beds and headboards, floating shelves in both live-edge and straight-edge styles, and specialty items. All pieces are handmade in the company's workshop, and the online catalog shows 42 items currently in stock. Woodrich also handles full commercial fit-outs, supplying furniture for entire restaurants, executive offices, rental properties, and hotels.

The customer base includes hospitality operators, commercial property managers, and residential buyers. Restaurant groups and hotel developers are cited as typical commercial clients, while the dining and bedroom collections serve individual homeowners. The company emphasizes that any customer design can be used as inspiration for a custom build.

Woodrich differentiates itself through its commitment to local sourcing and handmade construction, positioning each piece as a sustainable alternative to mass-produced furniture. The made-to-order model allows dimensions, wood species, and finish to be tailored per project, a capability promoted directly through the company's live chat and text channels.

about:
Woodshop QC operates in Charlotte, North Carolina, where it produces custom cabinetry and furniture for clients across the greater Charlotte area. The company does not publish a founding year or ownership structure, but client testimonials frequently reference team members Charlie and JP as key contacts.

The shop specializes in bespoke cabinetry and fine furniture, each piece handcrafted by artisans. Projects are developed through collaboration with custom builders, interior designers, and homeowners, and the company manages each job from design through installation. The website describes a process that begins with a project checklist and moves through design, construction, and final delivery.

Woodshop QC serves custom home builders, interior design firms, and individual homeowners. Testimonials cite completed projects such as kitchen cabinetry, family room built-ins, butler’s pantries, and a custom office desk, illustrating the range of residential applications.

The company states that it believes "creating from a standpoint of mere self-expression is insufficient" and that true artisans must create in ways that matter to other people. This philosophy underpins a collaborative approach intended to deliver pieces that reflect the client’s vision rather than the maker’s ego.

about:
Woonsocket Auto Salvage operates from Woonsocket, Rhode Island, where it has been family-owned since its founding in 1960. The business began as a local auto recycling operation and has remained under family stewardship for over six decades.

The company specializes in salvaging late-model and classic vehicles, maintaining over 20,000 square feet of indoor inventory stocked with thousands of new and used auto parts, including radiators, leaf springs, U-bolts, and a wide range of mechanical and electrical components. Approximately 1,500 salvage vehicles are on site at any given time. In addition to parts sales, the facility installs new and used auto glass. A parts-locating network powered by Car-Part Interchange and other locator services enables sourcing components across North America.

Woonsocket Auto Salvage primarily serves the auto recycling industry, supplying repair shops, collision centers, and individual vehicle owners throughout the United States and Canada. Its inventory spans mechanical assemblies, body parts, electrical harnesses, and emissions components, with extended warranties available on most items.

The company emphasizes its deep inventory, nationwide parts-locating capability, and warranty coverage as key differentiators, allowing customers to find hard-to-source components quickly and with confidence.

name: Workhorse Factory
old_description: Safe, proven school bus serving districts nationwide since 2013, with configurable seating for up to 14 students.
about:
Workhorse operates from its 400,000-square-foot manufacturing facility in Union City, Indiana, with corporate and engineering functions in Wixom, Michigan, and additional sites in Foster City, California, and Sharonville, Ohio. The company traces its commercial vehicle lineage to a school bus program launched in 2013, though a corporate founding year is not publicly stated.

The company engineers and manufactures intelligent electrical systems for mission-critical applications, producing commercial electric vehicles — including step vans and school buses — and a modular AI data center platform called TerraPod. Its Union City plant integrates industrial design, electrical, mechanical, and software engineering, testing and validation, supply chain management, and final assembly and quality testing. Real-world fleet experience exceeds 20 million miles, and a recent 200-unit order from Gateway Fleets demonstrates production scale.

Workhorse serves commercial fleet operators, school districts, defense and infrastructure markets, and the emerging distributed AI computing sector. Fleet customers operate across the United States and Canada; Gateway Fleets is a named operator expanding its electric step van fleet.

The company emphasizes that engineering and manufacturing under one roof, combined with millions of operational miles, allow it to turn complex technology into reliable products that meet gas- and diesel-truck expectations without compromise. Leadership cites pride in building the vehicles and equipment essential industries depend on daily.
